events.description: 8. ORDER denying: 3 "Motion for Preliminary Injunction." Plaintiff has not satisfied the requirements for relief under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 65. The pending Motion does not allege facts that, if true, would entitle Plaintiff to the extraordinary remedy of emergency injunctive relief. See Ross-Simons of Warwick, Inc. v. Baccarat, Inc., 102 F.3d 12, 18 (1st Cir. 1996) (noting that, under Rule 65(a), plaintiffs seeking preliminary injunctive relief bear the substantial burden "of demonstrating that a denial of interim injunctive relief would cause irreparable harm."). Accordingly, the Motion is DENIED without prejudice. Signed by Judge Maria Antongiorgi-Jordan on 2/4/2025. (ao) (Entered: 02/04/2025)

events.description: 38. ORDER denying: 37 "Supplemental Motion for Reconsideration." As explained at D.E. 36, the Court's basis for denying the early discovery requested by Plaintiff was and remains that Plaintiff has failed to demonstrate good cause for his request. The Court has re-reviewed Plaintiff's Motion for Discovery at D.E. 21, which fails to cite to a single case from the First Circuit nor any District Court therein. For the avoidance of doubt, the Court also reviewed Plaintiff's Reply at D.E. 34, which also failed to offer additional support for Plaintiff's request for early discovery. Plaintiff explicitly filed his Motion in "direct response to the Court's Order to Show Cause... [at] Dkt. No. 20 ." D.E. 21 at 1. Yet the Court has since vacated its Order at D.E. 20, and Plaintiff no longer faces any risk of failing to comply. Moreover, the information requested regarding FNU Ojeda has already been provided by Defendants. See D.E. 30 n.4. Plaintiff will be permitted to amend the Complaint at any point, so long as the request complies with the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure. Signed by Judge Maria Antongiorgi-Jordan on 5/16/2025. events.description: 47. ORDER granting: 39 "Motion to Dismiss." Under the Prison Litigation Reform Act ("PLRA"), incarcerated litigants are required to exhaust all available administrative remedies before bringing a lawsuit challenging prison conditions. 42 U.S.C. § 1997e(a) ("no action shall be brought with respect to prison conditions under... any Federal law, by a prisoner confined in any jail, prison, or other correctional facility until such administrative remedies as are available are exhausted."). This exhaustion requirement applies to federal prisoners suing under the Bivens doctrine, including Plaintiff. Porter v. Nussle, 534 U.S. 516, 524 (2002). Plaintiff, in both his original complaint and in the Amended Complaint at ECF 44-1, has failed to allege any facts suggesting that he has exhausted his available administrative remedies, as required by the PLRA. Rather, Plaintiff claims that he did not need to exhaust administrative remedies before bringing the instant suit, because no administrative remedies were "available" to him. Plaintiff fails to explain why he believes no administrative remedies were available to him; at most, Plaintiff states only that he was not provided with information about how to vote while in custody. (ECF 45 at 19). This allegation goes to the merits of his claims but in no way speaks to whether an administrative remedy program is available at MDC Guaynabo through which inmates can express grievances regarding unconstitutional prison conditions. In fact, Defendants have provided evidence that such a program does exist at MDC Guaynabo, in accordance with federal regulations 28 C.F.R. § 542.10542.19. (See ECF 30-1). Plaintiff has not disputed the availability of this program, and there is no evidence on the record suggesting that this program is unavailable to Plaintiff. The Court thus finds that Plaintiff was required to exhaust MDC Guaynabo's internal procedures before bringing his claims challenging prison conditions. Beyond the claims regarding prison conditions, Plaintiff has not stated any other claim upon which relief can be granted. The deficiencies in Plaintiff's complaint have not been cured by the filing of the Amended Complaint at ECF 44-1. The instant case is therefore DISMISSED without prejudice. Judgment shall be entered accordingly. Signed by Judge Maria Antongiorgi-Jordan on 6/12/2025. (ao) (Entered: 06/12/2025)
